\section[presentar]{presentar — to introduce; to present}

\label{lesson:ES-C502-presentar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the sign, then the Spanish for the fountain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: presentar}
\textbf{presentar} — \textquotedblleft{}to introduce; to present\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Te presento a mi amiga Ana.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Let me introduce my friend Ana.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Presentar un documento} — to hand in a document.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{presentar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{presentar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{presentar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the sign, then the Spanish for the fountain, then say \emph{presentar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does presentar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To introduce; to present\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: traducir}
\textbf{traducir} — \textquotedblleft{}to translate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Can you translate this message for me?}
\end{quote}

It takes \emph{zc} in the first person present: \emph{traduzco}.
